newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish union denies finances improperly managed.
newsitem.headline: Spanish union denies finances improperly managed.

text.p: Spain's Workers' Commissions (CCOO) union on Tuesday denied news reports that it suffered from gross financial mismanagement.

CCOO secretary for finance Jose Maria Diaz Ropero said remarks he made in a report on the state of the union's finances were taken out of context in an article published by financial daily Expansion on Tuesday.
"(The article) creates unjustified alarm over the economic situation of CCOO," Diaz told reporters. But he admitted improvements could be made in the management of finances.
According to Expansion, a review of CCOO's finances showed the union held more than 1,700 separate bank accounts over which it did not have full control.
Personnel was being hired by subsidiaries without the knowledge of the central organisation and the union was still counting the number of buildings it owned in Spain.
Diaz on Tuesday said the CCOO grouped more than 800 operations, each with their own budget, and all of whom were properly managed by their respective boards.
The report suggested efficiency could be improved by establishing a central budget, among other measures.
